gen_risks.description: Inexperience of SIS-SS with World Bank Procurement Regulations for consultancy contracts under the IPF component leading to selection and implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage procurement-skilled personnel, provide extensive World Bank handholding, utilize the STEP system, and apply World Bank prior/post reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risks related to the IPF component include the inexperience of the SIS-SS to process consultancy services following World Bank Procurement Regulations

gen_risks.description: SCERT Assessment Cell (SAC) has limited capacity and staff to design, administer, and analyze state Level Achievement Surveys and diagnostic assessments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a technical support agency through the IPF component to strengthen SAC staffing, institutional structure, and assessment capabilities.
gen_risks.evidence: The SAC has limited capacity and experience in these areas.

gen_risks.description: Delays in fund releases and low budget execution caused by complex multi-tier planning and limited budgeting capacity across agencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a financial management study, streamline AWP&B planning cycles, and deploy PFMS-linked Single Nodal Accounts for direct fund flows.
gen_risks.evidence: multiple tiers of planning and implementation and their limited capacities to prepare and manage budgets often result in inadequately planned budgeting

gen_risks.description: Systemic weaknesses in financial internal controls and persistent unresolved statutory audit observations dating back to FY 2009-10.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a formal Audit Committee, expand risk-based internal audit ToRs, and organize block-level camps to resolve legacy audit findings.
gen_risks.evidence: It may be noted that there exist unresolved/ addressed statutory observations since FY 2009-10.

gen_risks.description: Late approval of the Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) by the central Project Approval Board (PAB) delaying program execution start dates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre-finance ongoing and critical program activities through state budget allocations prior to formal PAB approval.
gen_risks.evidence: However, the AWP&B gets approved only by the third to the fifth month of the financial year.

gen_risks.description: Absence of annual procurement planning with structured timelines across implementing agencies causing procurement slippages.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate the publication of annual procurement plans within one month of AWP&B approval and mandate disclosure of awards on e-GP platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: the assessment found that there is no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan with timelines or of public disclosure

gen_risks.description: High dropout rates among adolescent boys at secondary and senior secondary levels due to economic pressures to enter informal labor.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop model composite schools offering science and commerce streams, introduce targeted remedial support, and build residential facilities for boys.
gen_risks.evidence: adolescent boys in secondary and senior secondary grades find it economically beneficial to drop out and take up informal jobs

gen_risks.description: Over-crowding in tribal hostels and lack of geographic needs-based planning leading to inequitable access for remote SC/ST communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct formal hostel need assessments, prioritize model composite school placement in SC/ST blocks, and strengthen SMC participation.
gen_risks.evidence: over-crowding of students in tribal hostels, (g) lack of geographic and needs-based planning to ensure equity and access

gen_risks.description: Enactment of new Personal Data protection legislation impacting project operations collecting and processing student and teacher data.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct technical impact analyses of new privacy legislation, adopt international data protection standards, and ensure anonymization of shared data.
gen_risks.evidence: approval of any new legislation regarding Personal Data protection may have an impact on the activities financed by the Operation

gen_risks.description: Vulnerability to climate extremes such as heatwaves, erratic monsoons, droughts, and floods forcing school closures and loss of instructional time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate disaster-resilient school designs, digitize student learning records, train principals in DRM, and deploy TaRL catch-up strategies.
gen_risks.evidence: The state is vulnerable to droughts and floods due to erratic monsoons and heat waves that can force extensions

gen_risks.description: Environmental, health, and safety risks during civil works, including poor fire safety, dust pollution, and lack of universal access features.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate environmental and social screening, integrate EHS obligations into standard bidding documents, and apply National Disaster Management safety guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: gap in following any fire safety norms in the schools, (c) lack of provisions for universal access to students and teachers

gen_risks.description: Staff vacancies in SIS-SS operating at roughly 70 percent capacity, limiting program implementation and monitoring oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract a Project Management Consultant (PMC) with dedicated fiduciary and E&S experts and execute a time-bound state staffing plan.
gen_risks.evidence: On average, SIS-SS is functioning at approximately 70 percent of the sanctioned strength.

gen_risks.description: Shortage of subject-specialist teachers forcing non-specialist language teachers to teach mathematics and science in multi-grade settings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured grade-specific lesson plans, transition to composite model schools with critical masses of subject teachers, and offer need-based CPD.
gen_risks.evidence: lack of subject teachers in schools managed by the GoCG has resulted in Language teachers teaching Mathematics, English, and Sciences.

gen_risks.description: Phased closure of coal mines due to long-term net-zero goals causing economic displacement in mining blocks and requiring workforce re-skilling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish at least 5 percent of model composite schools offering science and commerce education specifically in coal mining blocks.
gen_risks.evidence: India's long-term goal of reaching net zero by 2070... will result in the gradual closure of coal mines

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is rated Substantial. State elections are due in December 2023 and the associated large democratic exercise could slow down activities envisioned for the first year of the operation. The window between the operation being declared effective and the state elections is small.
gt_risks.mitigation: Disruptions are expected to be minimal given that the state intends to initiate work and complete necessary field work and/or data collection well before the elections, and utilize the election period for analysis and training module/materials development. The implementing bodies (SIS-SS, SCERT, SIEMAT, and SAC) will need to move swiftly to realize the state's plans.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design of operation risk is rated Substantial. Certain context-specific attributes such as topography and underlying community representation in overall enrolment could raise challenges, including barriers to school enrolment such as lack of physical access in sparsely populated areas with poor road connectivity, or high opportunity cost of schooling due to informal-sector employment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Government of Chhattisgarh has addressed similar challenges in the past through development and rollout of customized solutions; the project will enable planning for residential facilities for students and teachers in model schools in topographically hard-to-reach areas.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk is rated Substantial. In some cases, nodal educational institutions lack the expertise to implement technically complex interventions.
gt_risks.mitigation: Onboarding a Program Management Consultant (PMC) and technical support agencies is expected to significantly reduce the risks involved. Sustainability post-completion will be ensured through careful planning, technical support for capacity building of nodal institutions, and institutionalizing new mechanisms.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. Considering the implementing arrangements and diverse capacity across implementing agencies, implementation constraints can be foreseen in public financial management arrangements and compliance with rules and regulations for accountability.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focused attention in the short/medium term on enhanced effectiveness of planning, budgeting, and fund flow processes; adequacy of staffing and capacity building of fiduciary staff; strengthened monitoring through internal and external independent reviews; timely resolution of independent external review observations; a robust dedicated procurement complaints redressal system; strengthened contract management for delivery of goods and works; and ensuring exclusion of Bank-debarred firms from high-value contracts.
